inputs.share_count_basis: 833.6m equity shares outstanding at 30 June 2026 (Q1 FY27 6-K; FY26 diluted weighted average 833.33m, dilutive options 0.89m). 1 ADS = 1 equity share post the 1:5 split of 28 Oct 2024, confirmed by ADR/NSE parity in fx_note. Held FLAT: SBC (0.1% of revenue) is expensed in the flows, charging dilution too would double-count.
inputs.net_debt_note: 30 June 2026 (Q1 FY27 6-K 'Net Cash Surplus' table). total_debt = short-term borrowings 57,688 only; the Rs 14,264m of lease liabilities the company carries inside 'Loans and Borrowings' (71,952) is EXCLUDED because leases are charged as an operating cost in the flows (treatment B). cash = cash & equivalents 11,204 + investments 80,304 - restricted/unclaimed-dividend cash 102 = 91,406; equity investments at fair value (3,150) are kept IN because their FVTPL income is stripped from EBITDA (matching-asset rule). Company's own 'net cash surplus' of 30,568 excludes those equity investments; ours is 33,718.
inputs.interest_income_note: Finance income was Rs 7,870m in FY26 but is NOT inside reported OCF/FCF: Dr. Reddy's books interest and dividends received (1,521) in investing activities and reverses FVTPL fair-value gains (2,359) and net interest (12) out of operating cash flow. Deducting it again would double-strip. The company's reported EBITDA (PBT + net interest/investment income + D&A + impairment) likewise excludes it, so the EBITDA margin path is already ex-finance income and the cash+investments pile is counted once, in the bridge.
inputs.owner_fcf_note: last_fcf = reported FCF 18,330 (OCF 56,755 - PP&E 23,326 - intangibles 15,099) - SBC 326 - lease principal 1,263 - lease interest 802 = 15,939 (4.7% of revenue). FY26 includes the final two months of volume-capped lenalidomide plus Rs 4.5bn shelf-stock adjustment and Rs 3.5bn impairments; it is an anchor for the record, not the projection base -- the forward build is from components.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 20-F consolidated cash flow statement, 'Equity settled share-based payment expense' Rs 326m (FY25 424, FY24 407); no cash taxes on equity awards disclosed (net-share settlement not used). Filing units: Rs millions.
inputs.buyback_note: No treasury-share purchases in FY26 (Rs 1,389m in FY25, for ESOP trust). Dividend Rs 8/share (Rs 6,659m). The flat share count is funded: options are tiny (0.89m dilutive) and the ESOP trust buys shares for grants.
inputs.fx_note: USD/INR 96.30 (Yahoo INR=X, 2026-10-04T03:30Z); fx_rate 0.010384 = USD per INR (model -> quote). Parity: ADR 12.25 x 96.30 = Rs 1,179.7 vs DRREDDY.NS Rs 1,206.2 at the 2026-10-01 NSE close (NSE shut 2 Oct) -- ADR at a 2.2% discount, one trading day apart, confirms 1 ADS = 1 share and the rate direction. Replace the rate when refreshing the price; refresh_price.py moves the price only.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-02T20:00:02Z regular NYSE close (Friday); not an after-hours print
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in INR, the currency of the statements and the flows: 10y G-sec ~6.6% + beta 0.8 x India ERP ~6.5% = cost of equity ~11.8%; after-tax cost of debt ~5.3% on ~5% debt weight (short-term packing credit against a ~Rs 1tn market cap) -> WACC 11.5%. Roughly USD 8.5-9% after ~2.5-3% expected INR depreciation. Same WACC in all three scenarios: tariff, quality and lenalidomide risks are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate (charge risk once). Terminal growth 4.0% INR = Indian long-run inflation, zero real growth; cap 15x owner FCF for a generics business facing structural US price deflation.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost: FY26 lease principal 1,263 + lease interest 802 = 2,065 (0.61% of revenue) charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path (0.7% going forward, lease book grew to Rs 14.3bn at June 2026); lease liabilities EXCLUDED from total_debt; D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (20,605 - 1,702 = 18,903 = 5.6% of revenue) so the lease is not charged twice; cash tax on EBIT after that D&A.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated; the non-controlling interest (Nestle India's 49% of Dr. Reddy's and Nestle Health Science nutraceuticals subsidiary, NCI equity Rs 3,394m at 31 Mar 2026, loss share -384 FY26, -87 Q1 FY27) is deducted once in the equity bridge at book. Attributable-flows alternative not used because the JV is loss-making and immaterial (~Rs 4/share); FY0 consolidated profit 42,466 vs attributable 42,850 ties within noise. Equity-accounted associates (Rs 5,798m) are NOT added to the bridge because their profit share sits above PBT and is inside EBITDA.
inputs.ebitda_definition_note: Company EBITDA = PBT + net interest/investment (income) + depreciation + amortization + impairment. It is pre-impairment; impairments have recurred (3,519 FY26, 1,693 FY25, CAR-T/Eftilagimod/conjugated-estrogen write-offs) so every scenario's margin path is set ~0.5pp below the headline company EBITDA margin it corresponds to, as an allowance for recurring pipeline write-offs.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (routed via dcf-methods: operating company, non-US, with lenalidomide product-cycle cyclicality -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md; first valuation of this ticker, no MEMORY.md entry). Reporting currency INR (20-F IFRS statements in Rs millions), quote USD on the NYSE ADR. Mid-cycle construction: FY26 (22.8% EBITDA) and FY23-FY25 (27-30%) include volume-capped US generic lenalidomide, whose settlement caps expired 31 Jan 2026; North America revenue fell 51% YoY in Q4 FY26 and 35% in Q1 FY27 and the ex-lenalidomide run-rate is ~Rs 22bn/quarter against Rs 34-38bn in FY25. No scenario carries those margins forward: the base builds from the Q1 FY27 trough (12.5%, 15.4% ex the Rs 2.4bn semaglutide API charge) to 22.5% by FY31, which is the pre-lenalidomide FY19-FY22 range (22-25%) less the impairment allowance, and 0.5pp below management's 25% long-term target. Working capital: receivables + inventory - payables = 43% of revenue (June 2026), so growth consumes cash -- wc_capture is negative in every scenario. Capex: PP&E 23.3bn + purchased intangibles 15.1bn = 11.4% of FY26 revenue (biologics/peptide/injectable capacity plus product-right acquisitions), tapering toward 7% as the build-out completes; acquisitions of businesses (3,152 FY26, 53,096 FY25 for Haleon NRT) are excluded from capex and from the flows.

equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interest (Nestle India 49% of nutraceuticals JV) at book
equity_bridge.note: FY26 20-F balance sheet, 31 Mar 2026; Q1 FY27 NCI share of loss -87 makes the June figure ~3,307 -- immaterial, March audited figure used

historical_growth.owner_fcf_series_note: reported FCF (OCF - PP&E - intangibles) - SBC - lease principal - lease interest (IFRS 16 from FY2020; lease interest FY20-22 estimated at 150/200/250 from the 256/391/802 FY24-26 disclosures). Interest income not deducted: it is received in investing activities, outside OCF.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case 10-year revenue path average (FY27 +3% through FY36 +4%). Equity CAGR (17-18%) rejected: it compounds retained lenalidomide-era earnings and FY27 profit is running at a third of FY25's; revenue CAGR (11-12%) includes the FY25 Haleon NRT acquisition (+Rs 25bn inorganic) and lenalidomide.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 17.1% exceeds revenue 5yr CAGR 12.1% by >30% relative and EPS 3yr CAGR is -1.7% vs equity 3yr +18.1%: book value compounding reflects FY23-FY25 lenalidomide windfall retention, not sustainable earnings power. Owner FCF 5yr CAGR -5.9% vs reported -4.6%: SBC is flat but lease cash has tripled (482 -> 2,065), so a growing slice of reported FCF is lease-financed.
historical_growth.notes: SBC-adjusted FCF CAGR is below reported FCF CAGR only marginally (SBC is ~0.1% of revenue); the gap is lease cash under IFRS 16, not stock compensation.

base.growth_rationale: FY27 +3%: Q1 FY27 was -5.6% YoY (Rs 80.7bn) and Q2-Q3 still compare against lenalidomide-inclusive quarters; ex-lenalidomide base grew ~10% in Q1 and semaglutide supply resumes Nov 2026 (6-7m pens by March 2027, ~Rs 5-10bn) -> FY27 ~Rs 346bn, well below management's high-teens aspiration which requires a full semaglutide year. FY28 +10% on clean comps (India +12-14% vs IPM, Emerging Markets double-digit, Europe NRT, PSAI, semaglutide ex-India), then tapering 1pp/yr to 4% nominal INR.
base.margin_rationale: FY27 17.5% reported (Q1 12.5% incl. the Rs 2.4bn semaglutide charge; management ~20% ex-semaglutide for the remaining quarters). FY28 20%, FY31 22.5% = pre-lenalidomide FY19-22 range (22-25%) less 0.5pp recurring-impairment allowance; 2.5pp below management's 25% long-term target because US generics deflation (gross margin 58.5% -> 52.8% in FY26) and lower-margin NRT consumer mix offset India/EM branded growth.
base.capex_rationale: FY26 PP&E + intangibles 11.4% of revenue; biologics (Bachupally), peptide and injectable capacity plus product-right purchases taper to 7% (1.3x D&A at 4% growth). Cash tax 25% = FY26 cash tax paid / PBT (24.7%), India 25.17% statutory under the new regime.
base.wc_rationale: -40% of revenue change: net operating working capital (receivables 100.6bn + inventory 80.5bn - payables 37.5bn = 143.6bn) is 43% of revenue; FY24-FY26 WC consumed 40-60% of the revenue increase. Modest days improvement assumed as the inventory build for semaglutide/NRT launches normalises.

bull.rationale: Semaglutide resumes on schedule and scales across India, Canada, Brazil and other LoE markets (Rs 15-20bn FY27, a multi-year franchise); abatacept biosimilar approved in US/EU; NRT and India branded compound double digits; US tariff escalation on generics is deferred or waived; management reaches its 25% EBITDA target (24.5% after impairment allowance); capex normalises faster and working-capital days improve.

bear.rationale: Semaglutide relaunch slips past FY27 and the quality review widens (FDA 483s at Miryalaguda, Middleburgh, Srikakulam, Bachupally turn into warning letters / import alerts that delay abatacept); FY27 revenue -2%. US tariffs on generics escalate as scheduled in 2028-29 (FY29-FY30): North America (~26% of revenue) shrinks and margin compresses, growth stalls to 1% in FY30 and 3% thereafter; EBITDA margin plateaus at 19%, capex stays elevated for remediation and reshoring, working capital stays heavy. Terminal growth 3% INR (below inflation: real shrinkage of the US franchise).

scenario_narratives.base: Dr. Reddy's is an integrated Indian generics/API company whose FY23-FY26 profitability was inflated by volume-capped US generic lenalidomide; that settlement window closed on 31 January 2026 and North America revenue has reset from Rs 34-38bn to ~Rs 22bn a quarter. The base case treats FY27 as the transition year (revenue +3%, EBITDA 17.5% after the Rs 2.4bn semaglutide API charge in Q1), then lets the branded India (+12-14%), Emerging Markets/Russia, Europe NRT consumer and PSAI businesses plus a resumed semaglutide franchise carry growth of 10% fading to 4% nominal INR, with EBITDA recovering to 22.5% -- the pre-lenalidomide range, below management's 25% target. The axes are: how much of the 'double-digit base business' survives US generic deflation; whether semaglutide (the designated lenalidomide replacement) becomes a durable multi-market franchise after the July 2026 recall; and whether capex (11.4% of revenue) and working capital (43% of revenue) normalise so that owner FCF conversion rises from 4.7% to ~9% of revenue. US tariff escalation (exempt to 2028) is treated as a bear-case risk, not a base-case cost.
scenario_narratives.bull: Semaglutide supply resumes in November 2026 as guided and becomes a Rs 15-20bn franchise across India, Canada and other loss-of-exclusivity markets; abatacept IV is approved in the US and EU, establishing the biosimilars platform; NRT and India branded growth compound double digits; generic tariffs are deferred indefinitely; management hits its 25% EBITDA target by FY31 and the balance sheet's Rs 2bn M&A capacity is deployed at returns above WACC. Revenue grows 14% in FY28, 12% FY29, fading to 4.5%; owner FCF margin reaches ~11% as capex falls to 6.5% and working-capital days improve.
scenario_narratives.bear: The semaglutide quality failure is not a one-quarter event: the production pause extends, the FDA inspection findings across four sites escalate to warning letters or an import alert, and the biosimilar BLA slips. FY27 revenue falls 2%. In 2028-29 the scheduled 100%/200% US tariffs on generic imports take effect; management has said they cannot be absorbed and reshoring takes 4-7 years, so the North American franchise (26% of revenue) shrinks and group EBITDA margin plateaus at 19%. Capex stays at 8-10% for remediation and partial US manufacturing, working capital stays heavy, and terminal growth is 3% INR -- a real decline.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30%: three independent bear triggers are live at once -- an unresolved semaglutide API quality failure in the product meant to replace lenalidomide, Form 483s at four manufacturing sites in 2025-26, and a legislated US generic-tariff escalation in 2028-29 that management says cannot be absorbed. Bull cut to 20% because it needs semaglutide, abatacept, tariff relief and a 25% margin to all come through together. Base 50%: the ex-lenalidomide branded businesses are genuinely growing double digits and the balance sheet (Rs 33.7bn net cash) carries no solvency risk, so the central case is a slow margin rebuild, not distress.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the ex-lenalidomide business on owner free cash flow in INR, convert to USD at spot for the ADR. Owner FCF is reported FCF less SBC and the full lease payment; capex includes purchased product rights; working capital is a cash cost of growth; finance income stays out of the flows and the cash-and-investments pile is added once in the bridge. Margins are rebuilt from the Q1 FY27 trough toward the pre-lenalidomide range, never from the FY23-FY26 peak. Risk is charged in the scenario flows and weights, once, at a single INR WACC.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal margin: every 1pp of EBITDA margin in perpetuity is worth roughly Rs 40-45/share (~US$0.45); the base 22.5% is 2.5pp below management's stated target and 0.3pp below the FY26 reported figure that still contained two months of lenalidomide

Capex and working-capital normalisation: if PP&E plus intangible purchases stay at 11% of revenue and working capital at 43% of revenue with no days improvement, base owner FCF margin stays near 5% and the base value falls by roughly a third
US generic tariffs (exempt to 2028, scheduled 100%/200% after) are in the bear case only; a base-case cost would move the central value toward the bear value
Semaglutide execution: the July 2026 recall and production pause hit the single largest identified growth driver; a permanent loss of that franchise is the bear path

INR/USD: ADR holders bear ~2.5-3%/yr expected INR depreciation that the 11.5% INR WACC and 4% INR terminal growth embed; a faster depreciation lowers the USD value proportionally. Revenue is ~75% non-INR, so the operating hedge is partial
Band position: SBC is 0.1% of revenue so house and street values nearly coincide; the house/street band is ~Rs 5/share wide and band_position is not a meaningful statistic for this ticker

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (RDY, NYSE ADR) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 11.36-15.67 USD. FX from Yahoo INR=X and parity against DRREDDY.NS, see inputs.fx_note.
